O.outcome_detail: Patient outcomes, including mortality, complications, medication errors, shunt-surgery outcomes and patient satisfaction

result.effect: 14/19 studies reported no differences; 5/19 reported July-related adverse findings

cells.quote: Of the 19 studies evaluating a July effect, 14 mostly surgical studies reported no differences in patient outcomes compared with other months of the year (risk-adjusted) [16-20,22-26,31-34]. Of the five remaining studies, one study reported no difference in mortality in July, but potentially preventable complications did occur more often in July, although numbers were too small to allow for effective root cause analysis [27]. Another study reported a higher risk-adjusted mortality in July, which progressively decreased over the course of the year [21]. In a study on medication errors, the July effect could partially explain a spike of fatal medication errors [29]. One study reported a small July effect on outcomes related to cerebral shunt surgery in children and emphasized the need for supervision [28]. Another study showed a reduction in resident scores on a patient satisfaction questionnaire around July [30].
cells.note: The review synthesized heterogeneous observational studies and reported a mixed direction across outcomes.
